basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 13.' and it opens 'Vers. 13. Dixitque Cain: Major iniquitas mea quam ut veniam merear. Peccatis peccata'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 13. Dixitque Cain: Major iniquitas mea quam ut veniam merear. Peccatis peccata adjiciens desperavit, nec credidit se posse salvari vel veniam adipisci. Et | haec est blasphemia in Spiritum sanctum quae nec hic nec in futuro remittetur (Luc. XII, 10). Qui enim desperat, aut putat Deum nolle dimittere, aut non posse. Si non potest, non omnipotens, quia est aliquid quod non potest. Si autem non vult, quod etiam cogitare nefas est, invidet saluti humanae.
